info.name: Egoola API — Listing
info.description:
Admin Listing Management: product Listing CRUD + moderation (status + note + full history), **Gigs** (a seller's service offers, priced by packages: one SKU per price type), the listing/gig **Thumbnails**, and the Brand list that listings pick from.

Products, gigs and jobs are separate kinds with separate APIs: `/catalog/listings/` (products and, for now, buyer job requests) and `/catalog/gigs/`. A gig id on the listing endpoint is a 404 and a seller's service offer on it is a 400.

Key rules:
- Listings can be created by an Admin without a seller or buyer. Admin-created = `approved` by default.
- `listing_type: brand` requires `brand` = id of an active Brand (no free-text brand).
- `price` is the original price; `discounted_price` (optional, never higher than price; defaults to price) is the price charged — same on every price tier.
- `rejected` / `changes_requested` require `note`. `Listing.note` holds only the latest change's note (null if none); every change is kept in `status_change_logs`.
- Delete is soft for listings; a Brand used by any listing can't be deleted (409) — deactivate it.

How to use:
1. Pick the `Egoola - Local` environment (or edit `base_url`).
2. Run **Auth > Admin Login**.
3. Check the reference-data collection variables (`category_id`, `service_category_id`, `measurement_id`, `country_id`, `state_id`, `city_id`) — they must exist in your database.
4. Run **Brands**, **Listings**, **Gigs**, **Thumbnails** then **Cleanup** top to bottom ("Run collection") — each request saves the ids the next one needs.
5. "Update Listing — upload media" and the **Thumbnails** uploads need real files chosen in the Postman app; skip them in Newman.

See also: Egoola API — Category, Measurement, Seller and Accounts & Auth collections.

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin. Every Brand and Listing endpoint below is Admin-only.
Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life). Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.

Only `name` is required. `slug` is generated from the name and is unique across the whole project (a name whose slug already exists returns 400). `is_active` defaults to true. `created_by` / `creator_name` / `creator_type` are stamped from the Admin token and are read-only.
Creates a brand that cannot be picked by a listing (see 'Create Listing — inactive brand rejected').
Same name (or any name with the same slug, e.g. different casing) is rejected: "A brand with this name already exists."
The slug is regenerated from the new name. PUT works too but needs `name`.
Soft way to retire a brand that listings still use (a used brand cannot be deleted). Send `true` to re-enable.
Paginated. Filter by name with `?name=` (substring, case-insensitive).

query.description: general | used | village | retail | wholesale | brand

request.description: Lightweight rows only (no tiers / media / history) — those appear on Retrieve.

The admin's pending list: only `status = pending`, **newest request first** (`requested_at`), cursor pagination (`next` / `previous`, no `count`). Same filters as the list (`seller`, `catalog_type`, `listing_type`, `category`, `brand`, `created_from/to`, `requested_from/to`, `search`) and `ordering` (`requested_at`, `created_at`, `title`, `id`; `-` reverses). A listing a seller fixes after a rejection returns to the top. For a menu badge use `GET /catalog/listings/?status=pending&limit=1` and read `count`.

exec: pm.test('cursor shape: next / previous, no count', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('next'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('previous'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('count'); });

pm.test('only pending listings, newest request first', () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; r.forEach(x => pm.expect(x.status).to.eql('pending')); for (let i = 1; i < r.length; i++) pm.expect(new Date(r[i-1].requested_at) >= new Date(r[i].requested_at)).to.eql(true); });
pm.test('rows carry title_bn and requested_at', () => pm.response.json().results.forEach(x => { pm.expect(x).to.have.property('title_bn'); pm.expect(x.requested_at).to.be.a('string'); }));

request.description: Admin-created listing: **no `seller` and no `buyer`** is fine. Because an Admin creates it, `status` defaults to `approved` and one `status_change_logs` row is written. `listing_type: brand` makes `brand` mandatory — it must be the id of an **active** Brand (see the Brand folder), not a free-text name. `price` is the original price; `discounted_price` (optional, never higher than `price`) is the price actually charged; when you don't send it, it is set to `price`. The same two fields exist on every price tier.

exec: pm.test('3 tiers, tier discount saved (no discount -> equals tier price)', () => { pm.expect(b.price_tiers.length).to.eql(3); pm.expect(b.price_tiers[0].discounted_price).to.eql('120.00'); pm.expect(b.price_tiers[2].discounted_price).to.eql('130.00'); });

item.name: Moderation — approve (no note: Listing.note clears to null)

request.description: `Listing.note` always holds only the latest change's note — null here. Earlier notes stay in `status_change_logs`.

item.name: Moderation — note without a status change is ignored

request.description: A note belongs to a status change. Sent on its own it is ignored, so Listing.note always equals the newest status_change_logs entry.
`status` must be approved | rejected | changes_requested. Listings already at that status are returned in `skipped` (no history row); the rest in `updated`, one history row each.

exec: pm.test('pending one updated, approved one skipped', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.updated.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(b.skipped.length).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Repeat `media_file` once per file; `media_type` (image / video / document) is read from the file's content type. Remove files with JSON `{"media_delete_ids": [id, ...]}`. **Select real files by hand in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so this request returns 400 under Newman/CLI.

item.name: Retrieve Listing — status history and info change history

request.description: Two histories on the detail: `status_change_logs` (every status change with its reason) and `info_change_logs` (every content change by the seller or an admin: `changed_fields`, and `previous_data` / `new_data` with the same keys; prices, discounts and options are logged, stock is not). Both newest first.

exec: pm.test('has both histories', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status_change_logs).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; pm.expect(b.info_change_logs).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; });

pm.test('the earlier admin edit is logged with the admin as author', () => { const l = pm.response.json().info_change_logs[0]; pm.expect(l.creator_type).to.eql('admin'); pm.expect(l.changed_fields).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; });
pm.test('before and after have the same keys', () => pm.response.json().info_change_logs.forEach(l => pm.expect(Object.keys(l.previous_data).sort()).to.eql(Object.keys(l.new_data).sort())));
pm.test('has requested_at and Bangla fields', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('requested_at'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title_bn'); });

request.description: Soft delete: returns 204, the row stays in the database with `deletedAt` set and disappears from list/retrieve.
Admins can delete any listing (soft delete); sellers cannot.

A gig is a seller's service offer. It is priced by **packages**: one SKU per `price_type` (`hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `fixed`), `price` is the rate for that unit. A package has no duration: the buyer chooses it when ordering and pays the rate times it. No options, stock, brand or quantity prices. `catalog_type` and `posted_by_role` are set by the endpoint. An admin-created gig is `approved`; `seller` is optional.

exec: const by = {}; g.skus.forEach(s => by[s.price_type] = s); pm.collectionVariables.set('gig_hourly_sku_id', by.hourly.id); pm.collectionVariables.set('gig_weekly_sku_id', by.weekly.id);

pm.test('rates, and no duration on a SKU', () => { pm.expect(by.hourly.effective_price).to.eql('450.00'); pm.expect(by.weekly.price).to.eql('12000.00'); g.skus.forEach(s => { pm.expect(s).to.not.have.property('duration'); pm.expect(s).to.not.have.property('total_price'); }); });
pm.test('no stock, no options', () => g.skus.forEach(s => { pm.expect(s.stock_qty).to.eql(null); pm.expect(s.variants).to.eql([]); }));
pm.test('product-only fields are not part of a gig', () => ['brand','model','listing_type','measurement','price_tiers'].forEach(k => pm.expect(g).to.not.have.property(k)));

Brand, model, origin, warranty, measurement, condition, listing type, attributes, minimum order quantity and quantity prices are not available on a gig.

The gig endpoint only handles `service` / `seller_offer`; a different value is a 400.

Filters: `status`, `category`, `seller`, `price_type` (gigs with an active package priced that way), dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `search` (title, Bangla title, SKU code). Rows carry `price` / `price_type` of the lowest rate and `image_url`. Products are not in this list.
Packages, media, thumbnail, status history and the info change log.

exec: pm.test('is a service / seller_offer', () => { const g = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(g.catalog_type).to.eql('service'); pm.expect(g.posted_by_role).to.eql('seller_offer'); });

item.name: Create Listing — a product for the thumbnail demo

request.description: A small product to put a thumbnail on.

Upload or replace the gig's cover picture: multipart field `image` (JPG, PNG or WEBP, up to 10 MB). The previous file is deleted. It is not part of create or `PATCH`; `image_path` / `image_url` are read only elsewhere. **Select a real JPG / PNG / WEBP file by hand in the Postman app** (a shared collection cannot carry file paths, so this returns 400 under Newman). Do not set Content-Type yourself.

exec: pm.test('200 with a picture selected, 400 without (Newman has no file)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400]));

request.description: Pick a `.txt` or `.gif` file: only JPG, PNG and WEBP are accepted. (Under Newman, with no file, this is also a 400.)

exec: pm.test('200 with a picture selected, 400 without (Newman has no file)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400]));

request.description: The same endpoint shape exists for products. A gig id here is a 404. **Select a real JPG / PNG / WEBP file by hand in the Postman app** (a shared collection cannot carry file paths, so this returns 400 under Newman). Do not set Content-Type yourself.

exec: pm.test('200 with a picture selected, 400 without (Newman has no file)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400]));

request.description: `image_path` / `image_url` are `null` until a thumbnail is uploaded. A thumbnail change appears in `info_change_logs` as `thumbnail`.

exec: pm.test('has thumbnail fields', () => { const g = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(g).to.have.property('image_path'); pm.expect(g).to.have.property('image_url'); });

request.description: Removes the thumbnail and its file (`204`). Removing when there is none is also `204`.

item.name: Delete Brand — in use by a listing (expect 409)

request.description: A brand referenced by any listing — including soft-deleted ones — can't be deleted (409). Deactivate it with PATCH `is_active: false` instead.
